options.description: Edits wait only on a contradiction with what you confirmed, or on the intent loop's judge step. Other open questions are still asked right away but don't stop unrelated work.
options.label: Block only related edits (Recommended)

options.description: As on main today: while any judge question is open, all edits and writing commands wait, whatever they touch.
options.label: Any open question blocks

payload.question: When the judge blocks edits. The rule already blocks in the cases you mean. If a request reverses or extends something you confirmed, edits wait until you answer or type /plumb go. Inside a /plumb intent loop, nothing gets built until the judge step passes. What it removes is this: today an open judge question about some other record blocks every edit, even unrelated ones. That happened to me just now, which is why I'm asking. It also matches your 31 Oct answer, 'Ask at once, no block'. Keep it that way?
